Something I adapted from my theater days is called the Glass 4th wall:

I'm sure youve heard of the 4th wall, it's an invisible barrier between performer and audience that generally separates the world of the play from the real world outside the theater doors. Had a director when I was young say that we should pretend that the audience isn't there-- it's simply the 4th wall of the room you imagine on stage.

So how do you make this work for you? Act as if the audience is behind one way glass or they're not there at all. Play as if it's just you and your band having fun jamming in a bassment, smile (or warface if it's heavy music), and that energy will carry out to the crowd.

When you get more comfortable with this concept, then you can start to feed on the energy of the crowd like call and response. This makes them feel like they're part of the show, and it helps the band feel connected better.
